normalIntro.en: Keep the physical weapon in view, then let it travel into arguments and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 先盯住实物武器，再看它走进争论与医学。

normal.en: Weapon is the singular; arms is the plural collective.
normal.cn: weapon 是单数，arms 是复数集合。

normal.en: Weaponry is the mass noun for weapons as a whole.
normal.cn: weaponry 作为物质名词指全部武器。

normal.en: Weaponize means to make a weapon of something.
normal.cn: weaponize 是把某物做成武器。

normal.en: A weapon against a disease is a cure, not a gun.
normal.cn: a weapon against a disease 是疗法，不是枪。

normal.en: Information as a weapon is the commonest figurative use.
normal.cn: 信息作为武器是最常见的比喻用法。

abstract.en: Picture a spear leaning on cold stone.
abstract.cn: 想一支矛斜靠在冰冷的石上。

abstract.en: Feel the balance of a long shaft in one hand.
abstract.cn: 感受一只手握长杆时的重量平衡。

abstract.en: See a sign that says the spear was the first of its kind here.
abstract.cn: 看一块牌子写着这是此地出土的第一件。

examples.en: The police found a weapon in the car.
examples.cn: 警察在车里发现了一件武器。

examples.en: Education is a powerful weapon against poverty.
examples.cn: 教育是对抗贫困的有力武器。

examples.en: They accused each other of using gossip as a weapon.
examples.cn: 他们互相指责对方把流言当武器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威朋」——威朋把长矛靠在门口，说这是护家的第一件武器。

root: 日耳曼语 wǣpnam（战斗器具）→ 古英语 wǣpen → 中古英语 weapon；同源词有 weaponry、weaponize。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as one made object, widens to armed force, then turns to any means of winning or fighting.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一件制成品出发，扩大到武装力量，再转向任何取胜或对抗的手段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spear leaning against a stone wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支斜靠石墙的长矛。

branches.en: The object branch: weapons laid down at dawn.
branches.cn: 器物分支：黎明时放下的武器。

branches.en: The collective branch: talks on limiting weapons.
branches.cn: 集合分支：限制军备的会谈。

branches.en: The means branch: information in a campaign, a vaccine against illness.
branches.cn: 手段分支：竞选中的信息，对抗疾病的疫苗。

branches.en: The personal branch: patience as a negotiator’s weapon.
branches.cn: 个人分支：谈判者的耐心。

branches.en: The origin branch: an object held in the hand.
branches.cn: 起源分支：握在手中的器物。

intro.en: Weapon takes the ordinary noun and verb endings of English, chiefly in modern coinages.
intro.cn: weapon 采用英语常见的名词与动词词尾，主要用于现代新造词。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin source, so the Latin table stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 天气；气象；（使）风化；渡过（困难）
definition_en: the state of the air around us, and also to wear away by exposure or to come through a difficulty
core_image: 山顶一朵厚云被风推着压下来，山脊上的草一齐伏向一边
scene: 早上还是晴天，中午山那边压来一层低云，风把草全吹向一边，导游说下午会下雨。The weather turned in an hour, and the guide said rain was coming.
sceneCN: 这里 weather 是「天气」（第 1 个义项：空气的状态，晴雨冷暖）；句意为天气一小时就变了，导游说会下雨。被风推得低垂的云、一齐伏向一边的草就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 风里雨里；无论天气如何

senses.title: The state of the air
senses.definition: the condition of the atmosphere, such as sunshine, rain, wind and temperature
senses.definitionCN: 大气的状况，如晴、雨、风与温度
senses.example: The weather turned cold just before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期前天气变冷了。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense and the one taught first: what the sky is doing today.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常义，也最先教：今天的天空在做什么。

senses.title: Bad weather
senses.definition: rough or stormy conditions, often used with in or through
senses.definitionCN: 风浪大、天气差的状态，常与 in 或 through 连用
senses.example: The crew stayed in harbour until the weather cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们在港里等到天气转好。
senses.why: Sailors spoke of being in weather, and the plain noun took on the sense of a storm.
senses.whyCN: 水手说身处坏天气，这个普通名词就带上了风暴的意味。

senses.title: To come through a danger
senses.definition: to survive a difficult period, usually a storm or a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 度过一段困难的时期，常指风暴或危机
senses.example: The small firm weathered the recession better than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小公司比预期更好地熬过了衰退。
senses.why: Surviving a storm at sea gives the metaphor: to weather is to come out the other side.
senses.whyCN: 海上挺过风暴给出生动的比喻：weather 就是走到另一头。

senses.title: To wear away by exposure
senses.definition: to change or erode under sun, rain and wind over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间在阳光、雨水和风的作用下改变或被磨蚀
senses.example: The carving had weathered until the letters were faint.
senses.exampleCN: 石刻被风化得字迹模糊。
senses.why: Rocks that face the weather long enough simply become the verb.
senses.whyCN: 长期迎着天气的岩石，干脆把这个名词变成了动词。

senses.title: Of a ship, to pass to windward
senses.definition: of a sailing ship, to get past a point or a headland to the windward side
senses.definitionCN: 指帆船绕过某处或海岬，驶到上风一侧
senses.example: The ship weathered the cape at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 船在黄昏时驶过了海岬。
senses.why: To be weather of a cape is to pass clear of it, a nautical idiom now rare.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语意为一艘船安然绕过海岬，如今已是罕见的航海习语。

intro.en: Weather is an Old English word for the air and sky, related to wind, and it has been both a noun and a verb for a thousand years.
intro.cn: weather 是古英语中表示空气与天空的词，与 wind 有亲缘，一千年来既是名词也是动词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant wind and air, and related forms mean weather in German and Dutch.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根意为风与空气，德语与荷兰语中的相关形式也表示天气。

items.en: Weder meant air, sky and weather, and could also be used of a storm.
items.cn: weder 意为空气、天空与天气，也可指一场风暴。

items.en: The spelling settled as weather, and the phrase in weather came to mean in a storm.
items.cn: 拼写定为 weather，短语 in weather 转而指处于风暴中。

items.en: Seamen used weathering a cape for passing it, which grew into weathering a crisis.
items.cn: 水手用 weather a cape 表示绕过海岬，后来发展为 weather a crisis。

items.en: Geologists adopted weathering for the slow action of sun, rain and frost on rock.
items.cn: 地质学家采用 weathering 指日晒雨打霜冻对岩石的缓慢作用。

note.en: The first group shares the weather word or shape, the second names related conditions.
note.cn: 第一组与 weather 同词或形近，第二组指相关状况。

entries.definition: Worn by long exposure, or showing signs of age.
The slow wearing action of the elements.
Able to keep out wind and rain.
A word introducing a choice, not the air.
The usual pattern of weather over years.
A prediction of coming weather.
A period of violent weather.
To bear a difficulty to the end.

normalIntro.en: Weather is the sky in the morning and the rock after a hundred years, joined by the idea of facing something and coming through.
normalIntro.cn: weather 既是早晨的天空，也是百年后的岩石，中间由「迎着它并走过来」这一想法连接。

normal.en: Weather is what the sky does; climate is what it usually does.
normal.cn: weather 是天空此刻在做什么，climate 是它通常怎么做。

normal.en: Do not mix weather with whether, the asking word.
normal.cn: 不要把 weather 与 whether 混淆。

normal.en: In all weathers uses the plural for every kind of day.
normal.cn: in all weathers 用复数指各种天气。

normal.en: Weather the storm joins a noun of sky to a verb of survival.
normal.cn: weather the storm 把天空的名词与生存的动词连起来。

normal.en: Weathered stone is stone that has faced the weather a long time.
normal.cn: weathered stone 是长期迎着天气的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a cloth pulled by wind towards the ridge.
abstract.cn: 想一块布被风往山脊那边拉。

abstract.en: Feel the air turn colder just before rain.
abstract.cn: 感受下雨前空气忽然变冷。

abstract.en: See letters on a stone smoothed almost away.
abstract.cn: 看石头上的字被磨得几乎不见。

examples.en: The weather is fine, so let’s eat outside.
examples.cn: 天气不错，我们在外面吃饭吧。

examples.en: The company weathered two difficult years.
examples.cn: 这家公司熬过了艰难的两年。

examples.en: Wind and rain had weathered the statue’s face.
examples.cn: 风雨已经把雕像的面孔风化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威德」——威德先生每天看天，说天气就是风在德性上的脾气。

root: 日耳曼语词根（风、空气）→ 古英语 weder（天空、天气）→ 中古英语 weather；同源词有 windy 式的 wind、weatherproof。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the air above, hardens into a storm, becomes something to survive, and finally something that wears rock away.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从头顶的空气出发，硬化为风暴，成为要挺过的东西，最后成为磨损岩石的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloud driven down at a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：被压向山脊的云。

branches.en: The everyday branch: the weather turned cold.
branches.cn: 日常分支：天气变冷。

branches.en: The rough branch: waiting in harbour for the weather to clear.
branches.cn: 恶劣分支：在港里等天气转好。

branches.en: The survival branch: a firm weathering a recession.
branches.cn: 生存分支：熬过衰退的公司。

branches.en: The wearing branch: rock and a cape facing the wind.
branches.cn: 磨蚀分支：岩石与迎风的海岬。

branches.en: The origin branch: what the sky is doing today.
branches.cn: 起源分支：今天的天空在做什么。

intro.en: Weather compounds freely with nouns and adjectives, and takes the plain verb endings of English.
intro.cn: weather 与名词、形容词自由复合，并采用英语普通动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

items.example: It appears in weather the storm.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 weather the storm 里。

definition_zh: 编织；织（布）；编造；（穿行）蜿蜒
definition_en: to cross threads or strips over and under each other to make cloth, and also to move in and out of things
core_image: 梭子从一排绷紧的经线间穿过，把一根横线压进去，布面一点点长出来
scene: 老人坐在门口的木凳上，双手一推一拉，梭子来回穿过线阵，一块粗布慢慢铺开来。She wove with a steady shuttle, and the cloth grew under her hands.
sceneCN: 这里 weave 是「编织」（第 1 个义项：让线交错而成布）；句意为梭子来回穿行，布在她手下一点点长出来。穿过经线的梭子与逐渐成形的布面就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 编织；织布；编造；蜿蜒穿行

senses.title: To make cloth from threads
senses.definition: to cross threads over and under each other so that cloth or a mat results
senses.definitionCN: 让线彼此上下交错，织成布或席
senses.example: They weave wool into heavy blankets for winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把羊毛织成厚毯子过冬。
senses.why: This is the physical core: two sets of threads crossing.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：两组线交叉。

senses.title: To make something by crossing strips
senses.definition: to make an object by passing long strips over and under each other
senses.definitionCN: 把长条相互上下穿接，做成器物
senses.example: He wove thin reeds into a flat basket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把细芦苇编成一只扁篮。
senses.why: The same crossing action works on reeds and wire as on yarn.
senses.whyCN: 同样的交错动作，用于芦苇与铁丝，也用于纱线。

senses.title: To move in and out
senses.definition: to move along a winding path, passing between other things
senses.definitionCN: 沿弯曲路径移动，从其他事物之间穿过
senses.example: The road weaves between the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路在山丘之间蜿蜒穿行。
senses.why: A shuttle goes in and out of the warp, and a path may do the same.
senses.whyCN: 梭子在经线间进出，路径也可以这样走。

senses.title: To invent a story
senses.definition: to put details together into a story or an account
senses.definitionCN: 把细节拼合成故事或叙述
senses.example: She wove three old tales into one novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三个旧故事编进了一部小说。
senses.why: Strands joined into cloth give the image for details joined into a tale.
senses.whyCN: 线合成布，为细节合成为故事提供了意象。

senses.title: The pattern of a fabric
senses.definition: the way threads are crossed in a particular cloth, seen as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 某块布上线的交错方式，作名词
senses.example: The weave of the cloth is loose enough to let air through.
senses.exampleCN: 这块布织得够松，透得过气。
senses.why: The noun names the pattern that the verb produced.
senses.whyCN: 名词指动词所生产的那种纹样。

intro.en: Weave goes back to Old English wefan, a Germanic weaving word, and its irregular past wove and woven are the oldest forms.
intro.cn: weave 可上溯到古英语 wefan，是日耳曼语中的纺织词，不规则过去式 wove、woven 是最古老的形式。

items.en: The root is linked to an Indo-European word for weaving, seen also in Latin texere.
items.cn: 这一词根与印欧语中表示编织的词相连，也见于拉丁语 texere。

items.en: Wefan meant to weave, and the past forms wæf and wefen survive as wove and woven.
items.cn: wefan 意为编织，其过去式 wæf、wefen 留存为 wove、woven。

items.en: The verb kept its strong forms while gaining a weak weaved used for the winding sense.
items.cn: 动词保留了强变化形式，同时又长出弱变化 weaved，多用于蜿蜒义。

items.en: Weaving a story appears early, treating words as threads.
items.cn: 「编故事」很早就出现，把词语当作线。

items.en: Interweave and the textile noun weave spread the word into design.
items.cn: interweave 与纺织名词 weave 把这个词带入设计领域。

note.en: The first group shares the weave forms, the second the other verbs of making or winding.
note.cn: 第一组与 weave 同形同源，第二组是制作或蜿蜒的其他动词。

entries.definition: The ordinary past of weave.
Crossed threads turned into a finished cloth.
A person whose work is weaving.
To weave things into each other.
To make cloth from loops of yarn with needles.
To twist three or more strands together.
To follow a turning path.
To put parts together into a whole.

normalIntro.en: One crossing movement explains both the cloth and the winding road: something goes in and comes out again.
normalIntro.cn: 一个交错动作同时解释了布与蜿蜒的路：进去，再出来。

normal.en: Threads weave cloth; strips weave baskets.
normal.cn: 线织成布，条编成篮。

normal.en: The strong past is wove and woven; weaved suits winding paths.
normal.cn: 强变化过去式是 wove、woven；weaved 多用于迂回前行。

normal.en: A weaver is the person, weaving is the work.
normal.cn: weaver 是人，weaving 是活。

normal.en: Interweave means weave two things into one.
normal.cn: interweave 是把两样东西织在一起。

normal.en: Weaving a story treats words as thread.
normal.cn: weaving a story 把词语当作线。

abstract.en: Picture a shuttle sliding between tight threads.
abstract.cn: 想梭子在绷紧的线间滑过。

abstract.en: Hear the soft knock as each thread is pressed home.
abstract.cn: 听每根线被压紧时轻轻一响。

abstract.en: Watch cloth appear one line at a time.
abstract.cn: 看布一行一行出现。

examples.en: Villagers still weave baskets from local reeds.
examples.cn: 村民仍用本地芦苇编篮子。

examples.en: Our bus wove through the narrow streets.
examples.cn: 我们的车在窄巷里穿行。

examples.en: The cloth has a loose weave that keeps it cool.
examples.cn: 这种布织得较松，穿着凉爽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威乌」——威乌太太手一推一拉，梭子在「威乌」声里来回，布就织成了。

root: 印欧语编织词根（见拉丁 texere）→ 古英语 wefan（编织）→ weave，wov、woven 为保留的强变化形式。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with threads crossing, extends to strips, then to paths and to stories, and the noun names the pattern made.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从线交叉出发，扩展到长条、路径与故事，名词则指织出的纹样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shuttle crossing a warp.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过经线的梭子。

branches.en: The cloth branch: wool woven into blankets.
branches.cn: 布匹分支：羊毛织成毯子。

branches.en: The craft branch: reeds woven into a basket.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：芦苇编成篮子。

branches.en: The path branch: a road weaving between hills.
branches.cn: 路径分支：山路蜿蜒。

branches.en: The story branch and the noun: tales woven and the weave counted.
branches.cn: 故事分支与名词：编故事与织法。

branches.en: The origin branch: wool crossed over and under.
branches.cn: 起源分支：上下交错的羊毛线。

intro.en: Weave takes native verb endings and the prefix inter-, and keeps an irregular past.
intro.cn: weave 采用本土动词词尾与前缀 inter-，并保留不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere is the true cousin behind the weave images, so the table gives its family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 texere 是编织意象背后的亲族，故拉丁表给出其同族词。

definition_zh: 网；蜘蛛网；网络；（鸭、蛙的）蹼
definition_en: a net of fine threads spun by a spider, and also any network of connected parts, especially the internet
core_image: 清晨的蛛丝挂在枝叶之间，露珠一颗颗停在每个交点上
scene: 天亮后小路上挂着许多蛛网，露水停在丝的交点上，走过去时前额碰到一片凉。A web stretched across the path, strung with drops of dew.
sceneCN: 这里 web 是「蜘蛛网」（第 1 个义项：细丝结成的网络）；句意为一道蛛网横在小路上，挂着露水。挂在枝叶间、交点缀着露珠的蛛丝就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The net a spider spins
senses.definition: a fine net of threads spun by a spider to catch insects
senses.definitionCN: 蜘蛛吐丝结成的细网，用来捕捉昆虫
senses.example: A fly was caught in the web above the window.
senses.exampleCN: 一只苍蝇粘在窗上的蛛网里。
senses.why: This is the original sense: an animal-made net of threads.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：动物用丝结成的网。

senses.title: Any net of threads or straps
senses.definition: a woven or tied net, such as one used for carrying loads
senses.definitionCN: 用手工编结的网，如用来装运东西的网袋
senses.example: They carried the fruit home in a web of cord.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用绳网把水果扛回家。
senses.why: The same crossing structure is named for human-made nets.
senses.whyCN: 同样交错的结构，也用于人造的网。

senses.title: A network of connected things
senses.definition: a complex set of connected parts, people or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 由互相连接的部分、人或想法构成的复杂整体
senses.example: A web of canals links the villages.
senses.exampleCN: 纵横的运河把各村落连成一体。
senses.why: Lines meeting at many points look like a spider’s work at map scale.
senses.whyCN: 在许多点上相交的线，放大到地图尺度就像蜘蛛的作品。

senses.title: The internet
senses.definition: the system of linked pages and services accessed through the internet
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网访问的相互链接的页面与服务的总称
senses.example: Our school put the timetable on the web.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校把课程表放到了网上。
senses.why: Pages linked to pages repeat the spider’s image in electronic form.
senses.whyCN: 页面与页面相连，把蜘蛛的意象搬到电子世界里。

senses.title: The skin between toes
senses.definition: the skin joining the toes of a duck, frog or otter
senses.definitionCN: 鸭、蛙或水獭脚趾之间相连的皮
senses.example: The duck’s webbed feet pushed against the water.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭子的蹼在水里一推。
senses.why: The skin is a natural net, and English used its oldest net word for it.
senses.whyCN: 这层皮是天生的网，英语就用最古老的网词来称它。

senses.title: A weight or roll of paper
senses.definition: a large roll or sheet of paper made in one continuous piece
senses.definitionCN: 一次性制成的大卷或整幅纸张
senses.example: The press takes paper from a single web.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷机从一整卷纸中取纸。
senses.why: A continuous sheet of paper is spun and joined like a fabric, so printers call it a web.
senses.whyCN: 连续不断的纸幅像织物一样连成一片，印刷业便称之为 web。

intro.en: Web goes back to Old English webb, a word for woven cloth, which is also why the skin between a duck’s toes is called a web.
intro.cn: web 可上溯到古英语 webb，意为织成的布，这也正是鸭趾间那张皮被称为 web 的原因。

items.en: The Germanic root is the same one as weave, meaning a woven thing.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根与 weave 相同，指一件织成的东西。

items.en: Webb meant a piece of woven cloth and, by extension, any woven net.
items.cn: webb 指一块织成的布，引申为任何织成的网。

items.en: The spider sense became dominant because spider’s web was the everyday example.
items.cn: 蜘蛛义成为主流，因为蛛网是日常最常见的例子。

items.en: Web kept widening to canals, lies and other entangled structures.
items.cn: web 不断扩宽，用于运河、谎言等纠缠的结构。

items.en: In 1989 the World Wide Web gave the word its biggest modern extension.
items.cn: 1989 年万维网给了这个词最大的现代扩展。

note.en: The first group are web compounds of the computer age, the second the nets and tangles it resembles.
note.cn: 第一组是计算机时代的 web 复合词，第二组是它所比拟的网与纠缠。

entries.definition: A set of linked pages on the internet.
One page of a website.
Having skin between the toes.
Strong woven strips used in straps.
A mesh of cord for catching or holding.
A set of connected people, machines or roads.
The open spaces of a net, or the net itself.
A confused mass of threads or things.

normalIntro.en: Start with dew on a spider’s threads, then let the threads stretch to canals and to the internet.
normalIntro.cn: 从蛛丝上的露水开始，再让丝线延伸到运河与互联网。

normal.en: A spider’s web is made of threads the spider spins itself.
normal.cn: 蜘蛛网是蜘蛛自己吐丝结的。

normal.en: The Web with a capital letter is the internet system.
normal.cn: 大写的 Web 指万维网。

normal.en: Webbed feet are feet with skin between the toes.
normal.cn: webbed feet 是趾间有皮相连的脚。

normal.en: A web of lies is a set of lies all holding each other up.
normal.cn: a web of lies 是一张互相支撑的谎言网。

normal.en: A web of paper is one continuous width from the mill.
normal.cn: 纸的 web 是从造纸机出来的一整幅。

abstract.en: Picture a thread with one drop on each joint.
abstract.cn: 想一根丝、每个交点上一滴水珠。

abstract.en: Feel the cool line across your forehead.
abstract.cn: 感受额头上那一道凉丝。

abstract.en: See the same shape drawn over a map as roads.
abstract.cn: 看同样的形状被画在地图上成为道路。

examples.en: The garden was full of webs after the wet night.
examples.cn: 潮湿的夜里过后，花园里到处是蛛网。

examples.en: She typed the address into the web browser.
examples.cn: 她把地址输进网页浏览器。

examples.en: The old city is a web of narrow lanes.
examples.cn: 老城是一片纵横的窄巷网。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「韦布」——韦布老先生清早出门，一头撞进挂满露水的蛛网。

root: 日耳曼语编织词根 → 古英语 webb（织成的织物、网）→ 中古英语 web；同源词有 weave、webbed。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as woven cloth and thread, then net, then any connected structure, ending with the internet and even a roll of paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从织成的布与线出发，到网，再到任何互相连接的结构，最后到互联网甚至整卷纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spider’s web strung with dew.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂着露水的蛛网。

branches.en: The spider branch: a fly caught above the window.
branches.cn: 蜘蛛分支：粘在窗上的苍蝇。

branches.en: The craft branch: a cord net for fruit.
branches.cn: 手工分支：装水果的绳网。

branches.en: The network branch: canals linking villages and pages linking pages.
branches.cn: 网络分支：连通村落的运河与互相链接的页面。

branches.en: The bodily and paper branch: webbed feet and a roll of paper.
branches.cn: 身体与纸张分支：蹼足与整卷纸。

branches.en: The origin branch: a spider spinning above the window.
branches.cn: 起源分支：在窗上结网的蜘蛛。

intro.en: Web compounds very freely in modern English, above all in computing.
intro.cn: web 在现代英语中极能复合，尤其在计算机领域。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin table is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 web browser 里。

definition_zh: 婚礼；结婚庆典；结婚纪念
definition_en: a ceremony at which two people marry, and the celebration that follows it
core_image: 一对手挽手从铺满花瓣的门廊走出来，身后是散落的白花和掌声
scene: 院子里的长桌铺着白布，亲戚们从各地赶来，新人从花门下走过时大家一齐起身。Relatives came from three provinces to the wedding in the courtyard.
sceneCN: 这里 wedding 是「婚礼」（第 1 个义项：两人结婚的仪式与庆典）；句意为亲戚们从三省赶来参加院中的婚礼。手挽手走过花门下、身后落满白花的两人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 婚礼；结婚庆典；结婚纪念

senses.title: The marriage ceremony
senses.definition: the formal ceremony in which two people become husband and wife
senses.definitionCN: 两人正式结为夫妻的仪式
senses.example: The wedding will be held in a small country church.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼将在一座乡下小教堂举行。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the ceremony itself, from the verb wed.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：仪式本身，来自动词 wed。

senses.title: The whole celebration
senses.definition: the party or feast that follows the ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 仪式之后的宴会与庆祝
senses.example: The wedding went on until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼庆典一直持续到半夜。
senses.why: In everyday speech the ceremony and the party blur into one word.
senses.whyCN: 在日常说法里，仪式与宴会合成一个词。

senses.title: A wedding anniversary
senses.definition: used with an ordinal to name a year of marriage, usually silver or golden
senses.definitionCN: 与序数词连用指结婚周年，常见金婚、银婚
senses.example: They are celebrating their golden wedding this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天他们要庆祝金婚。
senses.why: An anniversary repeats the wedding date, so the word for the event names the year too.
senses.whyCN: 纪念日重复的是婚礼那一天，于是事件的词也成了纪年的词。

senses.title: Of or for a marriage
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe things made for a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指为结婚而备的东西
senses.example: She borrowed her sister’s wedding dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她借了姐姐的婚纱。
senses.why: The participle form simply labels objects by the event they belong to.
senses.whyCN: 分词形式只是用所属事件来标记物件。

senses.title: A joining of anything
senses.definition: in literary use, a close union of two ideas, groups or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 在书面用法中指两种理念、团体或品质的紧密结合
senses.example: The design is a wedding of old brick and new glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计是旧砖与新玻璃的结合。
senses.why: Two things joined as closely as a married pair are said to be wedded.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西结合得如夫妻一般，就说它们被「婚配」了。

intro.en: Wedding came from the Old English verb weddian, to pledge, and it once meant the pledge itself rather than the party.
intro.cn: wedding 来自古英语动词 weddian（立誓），起初指誓言本身，而非庆典。

items.en: Weddian meant to pledge or to promise, especially by giving a surety.
items.cn: weddian 意为立誓、许诺，尤指以担保物作保。

items.en: The noun wedding first named the act of pledging and the pledge given.
items.cn: 名词 wedding 最初指立誓的行为与所立的誓约。

items.en: Because a marriage was sealed by a pledge, the word settled on the marriage rite.
items.cn: 由于婚姻以誓约缔结，这个词便固定用于结婚仪式。

items.en: The -ing ending became a plain noun, and the plural weddings appeared.
items.cn: 词尾 -ing 成了普通名词标志，复数 weddings 随之出现。

items.en: Gold and silver wedding extended the word to anniversaries.
items.cn: golden wedding、silver wedding 把词意扩展到结婚纪念。

note.en: The first group is the wedding family, the second the other words for marrying.
note.cn: 第一组是 wedding 词族，第二组是表示结婚的其他说法。

entries.definition: To marry, or to join closely.
Married, or devoted to something.
Not married.
The day of a marriage.
The legal state of being husband and wife.
A formal set of acts for an occasion.
The woman who is marrying.
A joyful event held to mark something.

normalIntro.en: A wedding was once a promise, not a party: keep the pledge in view and the word explains itself.
normalIntro.cn: wedding 本来是一个许诺而不是一场宴席：记住「立誓」，这个词就不难了。

normal.en: Wed is the verb; wedding is the ceremony.
normal.cn: wed 是动词，wedding 是仪式。

normal.en: Wedding day is the day; wedding ring is the ring.
normal.cn: wedding day 是一天，wedding ring 是一只环。

normal.en: Golden wedding and silver wedding are anniversaries.
normal.cn: golden wedding 与 silver wedding 都是结婚纪念。

normal.en: Wedding dress and wedding cake take the word before the noun.
normal.cn: wedding dress 与 wedding cake 把词放在名词之前。

normal.en: To wed two ideas is to join them like a couple.
normal.cn: to wed two ideas 是把两种想法像夫妻一样结合。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking under a flower arch.
abstract.cn: 想两个人从花门下走过。

abstract.en: Hear chairs scrape back as the guests rise.
abstract.cn: 听椅子挪动、宾客一同起身。

abstract.en: Feel white petals underfoot in the doorway.
abstract.cn: 感受门廊下脚底的白花瓣。

examples.en: Their wedding was small, with only family present.
examples.cn: 他们的婚礼很小，只请了家人。

examples.en: He put the wedding ring back in its box.
examples.cn: 他把婚戒放回盒子里。

examples.en: The room is a wedding of modern steel and old wood.
examples.cn: 这个房间是现代钢与旧木的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威丁」——威丁两口子挑了个晴天，在院里的花门下把誓言说了一遍。

root: 古英语 weddian（立誓、以担保物许诺）→ 名词 wedding（立誓、婚约）→ 中古英语后固定为婚礼；同源词有 wed、wedded。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a pledge, settles on the rite, widens to the party, and can label a union of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从誓约出发，落到仪式上，扩展到宴庆，最后可指任何结合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a couple stepping out under a flower arch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一对新人从花门下走出。

branches.en: The rite branch: a small country church.
branches.cn: 仪式分支：乡下的小教堂。

branches.en: The party branch: dancing until midnight.
branches.cn: 宴庆分支：跳舞到半夜。

branches.en: The anniversary and object branch: a golden wedding and a borrowed dress.
branches.cn: 纪念与物件分支：金婚与借来的婚纱。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: brick joined with glass.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：砖与玻璃的结合。

branches.en: The origin branch: the pledge that came first.
branches.cn: 起源分支：最先存在的誓约。

intro.en: Wedding is a gerund that became a plain noun, and it compounds easily with wedding-day words.
intro.cn: wedding 是动名词转成的普通名词，容易与婚礼相关词复合。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 星期三；周三
definition_en: the day of the week after Tuesday and before Thursday
core_image: 挂历翻到第三挡，手指点在中间那一格，一周过半
scene: 课表上那个空格填着「周三 下午 实验」，学生每到这天才把实验服带来。We have lab work every Wednesday afternoon this term.
sceneCN: 这里 Wednesday 是「星期三」（第 1 个义项：一周中的第三天，周二之后、周四之前）；句意为这学期每周三下午做实验。翻到中间那一格的挂历就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 圣灰星期三（四旬期首日）

senses.title: The fourth day of the week
senses.definition: the day between Tuesday and Thursday, the fourth in the usual Monday-first week
senses.definitionCN: 周二与周四之间的那一天，通常以周一开头计为第四天
senses.example: The meeting has been moved to Wednesday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议改到星期三下午。
senses.why: This is the ordinary sense, a fixed slot in the seven-day cycle.
senses.whyCN: 这是普通义：七日循环中的固定一格。

senses.title: A name used for dates
senses.definition: used with a date or month to fix a meeting, as on Wednesday 12 May
senses.definitionCN: 与日期或月份连用以确定某天，如 5 月 12 日星期三
senses.example: The hearing will be on Wednesday 12 May at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 听证将于 5 月 12 日星期三十时举行。
senses.why: In schedules the day word pins a date, and English writes it before the number.
senses.whyCN: 在日程中这个日名词被用来锁定日期，英语把它写在数字之前。

senses.title: A day marked by an observance
senses.definition: appears in names of observances such as Ash Wednesday
senses.definitionCN: 出现在 Ash Wednesday 这类节日名称中
senses.example: Many parishioners wear ashes on Ash Wednesday.
senses.exampleCN: 许多教区居民在圣灰星期三涂灰。
senses.why: Church calendars attach a fixed feast to the day name, so the word can carry the festival.
senses.whyCN: 教会日历把一个固定节日挂在这天名字上，词就带上了节日。

senses.title: Repeatedly, on Wednesdays
senses.definition: the plural or with -s used adverbially, as in she works Wednesdays
senses.definitionCN: 复数或加 -s 作副词，如她每周三上班
senses.example: The shop closes early Wednesdays.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店每周三提前关门。
senses.why: English marks a weekly habit with the plural day word, without a preposition.
senses.whyCN: 英语用复数日名表示每周习惯，不加介词。

senses.title: The middle of the working week
senses.definition: informally used as a midpoint reference, as in Wednesday of a conference
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用作中点的参照，如会议的第三天
senses.example: By Wednesday the team was already behind.
senses.exampleCN: 到星期三时，团队已经落后了。
senses.why: In a working week this day marks the halfway point, so it often ranks things.
senses.whyCN: 在工作周里这一天标志中点，因此常被用来划分进程。

intro.en: Wednesday is Woden’s day, the English name given by Anglo-Saxon speakers to the Roman day of Mercury.
intro.cn: Wednesday 是「沃登之日」，盎格鲁-撒克逊人用它来对应罗马人的水星日。

items.en: When Germanic peoples adopted the seven-day week, they replaced planet gods with their own deities.
items.cn: 日耳曼民族接受七日周时，用自己的神取代了行星之神。

items.en: Wōdnesdæg meant the day of Woden, the chief god of the Old English pantheon.
items.cn: wōdnesdæg 意为沃登之日，沃登是古英语诸神之首。

items.en: The word was already spelled and spoken with a swallowed d, as Wennesday.
items.cn: 中古英语中这个词的 d 已读得含糊，写作 Wennesday。

items.en: Spelling kept the d long after the sound vanished in the usual pronunciation.
items.cn: 现代拼写保留了 d，但通常发音里这个音早已消失。

items.en: Woden also stands behind Odin, the Norse name of the same god.
items.cn: 沃登也是挪威神话中奥丁这一名字的来源，两者是同一个神。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like Wednesday, the second are its fellow days.
note.cn: 第一组与 Wednesday 形近或音近，第二组是同一周中的其他日名。

entries.definition: More than one Wednesday, or every Wednesday.
The written short form.
The Old English god inside the word.
The day named for Tiw, before Wednesday.
The day before Wednesday.
The day after Wednesday.
Wednesday or the middle of the week.
Any working day from Monday to Friday.

normalIntro.en: Say it as Wenns-day: the d is written but never spoken, and that is the only real trap.
normalIntro.cn: 读作 Wenns-day：d 只写不读，这是唯一的真陷阱。

normal.en: Write Wednesday with a d, say it without one.
normal.cn: 拼写有 d，读音没有 d。

normal.en: The middle letters are nes, not news.
normal.cn: 中间是 nes，不是 news。

normal.en: Woden gives the Wed- part, as he gives Odin in Norse.
normal.cn: Wed- 来自沃登，正如奥丁也是他。

normal.en: On Wednesday, not in Wednesday.
normal.cn: 用 on Wednesday，不用 in。

normal.en: Wednesdays without a preposition means every week.
normal.cn: 不带介词的 Wednesdays 意为每周三。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with the middle box ringed.
abstract.cn: 想日历中间那一格被圈起来。

abstract.en: Hear the short sound wen, like when without the i.
abstract.cn: 听那个短音 wen，像 when 去掉 i。

abstract.en: Feel the week tilt forward from that day.
abstract.cn: 感受一周从这天起向周末倾斜。

examples.en: I will see you on Wednesday morning.
examples.cn: 我们星期三上午见。

examples.en: She plays tennis Wednesdays after work.
examples.cn: 她每周三下班后打网球。

examples.en: The letter arrived on Wednesday 3 June.
examples.cn: 信在 6 月 3 日星期三到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温斯得」——温斯太太每到周三都说「得」去开会，嘴上却不读那个 d。

root: 古英语 wōdnesdæg（沃登之日）→ 中古英语 Wennesday → Wednesday；同源神话名有 Odin。

sensesIntro.en: The word names one fixed day, then works as a date marker, a festival name and a way to say every week.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指一周中固定的一天，再用作日期标记、节日名与「每周」的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger on the middle box of a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指点在日历中间那一格。

branches.en: The plain day branch: a meeting moved to this day.
branches.cn: 日常分支：会议改到这天。

branches.en: The dating branch: on Wednesday 12 May.
branches.cn: 计日分支：5 月 12 日星期三。

branches.en: The observance branch: ashes and a special service.
branches.cn: 节日分支：涂灰与特别礼拜。

branches.en: The habitual branch: early closing every week.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：每周提前关门。

branches.en: The origin branch: Woden, the god in the name.
branches.cn: 起源分支：名字中的沃登神。

intro.en: Wednesday is a compound of a god’s name and day, and its endings are the ordinary plural and possessive.
intro.cn: Wednesday 是神名加 day 的复合词，词尾只是普通的复数与所有格。

latinIntro.en: The Latin day name dies Mercurii shows the planet model that English replaced, so the table records it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁日名 dies Mercurii 显示了被英语替换的行星模型，故拉丁表列出它。

definition_zh: 杂草；野草；菸草（口语）；除草
definition_en: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted, and also to remove such plants
core_image: 菜畦里一丛比菜苗还壮的野草，被人一把连根拔起
scene: 雨后的菜畦里，野草长得比菜苗还高，母亲蹲下把它们一株株拔起来。After the rain the weeds stood taller than the young vegetables, so we pulled them out.
sceneCN: 这里 weed 是「杂草」（第 1 个义项：长在不该长地方的野生植物）；句意为雨后野草比菜苗还高，我们把它拔掉。比菜苗还壮、被连根拔起的那丛草就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A plant in the wrong place
senses.definition: a wild plant growing where people do not want it
senses.definitionCN: 长在人们不需要的地方的野生植物
senses.example: Dandelions are a weed in a lawn and a flower in a meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 蒲公英在草坪上是杂草，在草甸上是花。
senses.why: This is the core sense, and it depends on place rather than species.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，取决于位置而非种类。

senses.title: To remove such plants
senses.definition: to pull out or cut unwanted plants from a garden or field
senses.definitionCN: 从园圃或田地里拔掉或割掉不受欢迎的植物
senses.example: They weeded the beds before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们到来之前，他们把花坛的草清干净了。
senses.why: Once the noun named the plant, the verb named the work.
senses.whyCN: 名词指草之后，动词就指拔草这件事。

senses.title: To remove unwanted things or people
senses.definition: to get rid of weak or unwanted members from a group
senses.definitionCN: 从群体中清掉弱的或不需要的成员
senses.example: The first round weeds out the weakest entries.
senses.exampleCN: 第一轮会淘汰最弱的参赛作品。
senses.why: Pulling weak plants out of a bed gives the image for clearing a list.
senses.whyCN: 把弱苗从苗床里拔掉，为清理名单提供了意象。

senses.title: Tobacco, in informal use
senses.definition: an old slang word for tobacco or a cigarette
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中指菸草或香烟
senses.example: He stepped outside for a weed.
senses.exampleCN: 他走到外面抽支烟。
senses.why: This slang sense is old and has almost disappeared from polite speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一俚语义已陈旧，在正式场合几乎绝迹。

senses.title: A troublesome person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as a nuisance, in slang
senses.definitionCN: 口语中令人讨厌的人或事
senses.example: That old car is a weed of a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车真是台麻烦机器。
senses.why: Something that grows where it is not wanted and will not go away suits both plants and pests.
senses.whyCN: 在不该生长的地方长起来又除不掉的东西，既像草也像麻烦。

intro.en: Weed is an Old English word for a harmful herb, and it once carried the sense of something poisonous or worthless.
intro.cn: weed 是古英语中表示有害草木的词，曾带有「有毒、无用」的意味。

items.en: Wēod meant a herb, especially a harmful one growing among crops.
items.cn: wēod 意为草木，尤指长在作物间的有害草木。

items.en: Related forms in Dutch and German also mean weed, so the sense is very old.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语中的相关形式也表示杂草，可见这个意义很古老。

items.en: Spelling settled as weed and the garden sense became fixed.
items.cn: 拼写定为 weed，园艺义随之固定。

items.en: Weed out grew from garden work into any clearing of a group.
items.cn: weed out 从园艺劳动扩展到对任何群体的清理。

items.en: Slang uses for tobacco and for a tiresome person came and mostly went.
items.cn: 指菸草与讨厌之人的俚语用法出现过，又多半消散。

note.en: The first group shares the weed word, the second names plants and clearing work.
note.cn: 第一组与 weed 同词同源，第二组指植物与清理工作。

entries.definition: Full of weeds, or thin and weak.
Plant-like growth in the sea.
A substance that kills weeds.
The work of removing weeds.
The common green ground plant, wanted on lawns.
Any living green thing that grows in soil.
A plant used for food or medicine.
Loosening soil and cutting weeds with a hoe.

normalIntro.en: A weed is not a kind of plant but a plant in the wrong place, which is why the verb can also mean to clear a list.
normalIntro.cn: 杂草不是某个种类，而是长错地方的植物，所以动词也能表示清理名单。

normal.en: Weed is both the plant and the pulling of it.
normal.cn: weed 既是草，也是拔草。

normal.en: Weed out means remove the weak ones.
normal.cn: weed out 意为剔除弱者。

normal.en: Weedy grounds are full of weeds; a weedy person is thin.
normal.cn: weedy 地面满是草，weedy 的人很瘦。

normal.en: Seaweed is not a garden pest at all.
normal.cn: seaweed 根本不是园中害虫。

normal.en: Weedkiller is what stops you weeding by hand.
normal.cn: weedkiller 让你不必动手拔草。

abstract.en: Picture a thistle standing higher than lettuce.
abstract.cn: 想一株飞蓟比生菜还高。

abstract.en: Feel the root come free with a quick tug.
abstract.cn: 感受一拽根部就松脱。

abstract.en: Smell the crushed green on your hands.
abstract.cn: 闻手上碾碎的青草味。

examples.en: The path is overgrown with weeds.
examples.cn: 这条小路上长满杂草。

examples.en: He spent the morning weeding the vegetable beds.
examples.cn: 他花了一上午给菜畦除草。

examples.en: The test is meant to weed out careless applicants.
examples.cn: 这项测试意在淘汰粗心的申请者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威得」——威得大叔蹲在菜地，一根根拔得干净，说这些都是抢营养的杂草。

root: 古英语 wēod（草本，尤指有害草木）→ 中古英语 weed；同源词有 weedy、seaweed。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a plant out of place, becomes the work of removing it, then any clearing of unwanted members.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从长错地方的植物出发，成为清除它的劳动，再指任何对多余成员的清理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weed pulled up by the root.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株被连根拔起的草。

branches.en: The plant branch: dandelions in a lawn.
branches.cn: 植物分支：草坪上的蒲公英。

branches.en: The work branch: beds weeded before guests came.
branches.cn: 劳动分支：客人来前清好的花坛。

branches.en: The bed branch: beds weeded before guests came.
branches.cn: 苗床分支：客人来前清好的花坛。

branches.en: The clearing branch: a test that weeds out the careless.
branches.cn: 清理分支：淘汰粗心者的测试。

branches.en: The slang branch: an old word for a cigarette or a nuisance.
branches.cn: 俚语分支：旧时指香烟或讨厌之物。

intro.en: Weed takes the ordinary English endings for its plural and its verb forms.
intro.cn: weed 的复数与动词形式采用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

items.meaning: more than one, or he weeds

definition_zh: 星期；周；一周（工作周）；七天的期间
definition_en: a period of seven days, usually counted from Monday to Sunday, and also the working days in it
core_image: 墙上挂历被撕下七页，边缘参差，露出新的一周
scene: 宿舍墙上挂着一本薄薄的日历，每过一天撕一页，撕下七页就在下面写一行小结。She tore off a page a day, and every week ended with a line of notes.
sceneCN: 这里 week 是「星期」（第 1 个义项：七天的期间）；句意为她每天撕一页，每周结束时写一行小结。被撕下七页、边缘参差的挂历就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 星期；周；工作周；一周的期间

senses.title: Seven days
senses.definition: a period of seven days, counted from a fixed day or from any day
senses.definitionCN: 从固定一日或任意一日算起的七天
senses.example: The course lasts six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课持续六个星期。
senses.why: This is the basic unit: a run of seven days.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本单位：连续七天。

senses.title: A calendar week
senses.definition: the seven days from Monday to Sunday as marked on a calendar
senses.definitionCN: 日历上从周一到周日的七天
senses.example: The report is due by the end of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在本周末前到期。
senses.why: For schedules people count from Monday, giving the week a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 在日程安排中人们从周一数起，给一周一个固定框架。

senses.title: The working week
senses.definition: the days set aside for work, usually Monday to Friday
senses.definitionCN: 用于工作的那些日子，通常为周一到周五
senses.example: She works a four-day week.
senses.exampleCN: 她一周工作四天。
senses.why: From the seven days the word narrows to the days that count as work.
senses.whyCN: 从七天缩窄到算作工作的那些天。

senses.title: The week as a business period
senses.definition: the period a business or paper treats as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 商家或报刊所算作一个单位的期间
senses.example: This week we have three new offers.
senses.exampleCN: 本周我们有三项新的优惠。
senses.why: Traders cut the continuous cycle into weeks for counting sales and notices.
senses.whyCN: 商家把连续的循环切成周，用来计算销量与公告。

senses.title: Weak in compounds
senses.definition: used in compounds such as weekday, weekend and midweek to place events
senses.definitionCN: 用于 weekday、weekend、midweek 等复合词，标定时间位置
senses.example: Plans change at weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末的时候计划会变。
senses.why: Compounds let one word locate any event within the cycle.
senses.whyCN: 复合词让一个词把事情放到循环中的某处。

intro.en: Week is a Germanic word for a period of seven days, replacing an older English word of the same meaning.
intro.cn: week 是日耳曼语中表示七天的词，取代了同义的古英语旧词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant a turn or a series, and was applied to the cycle of days.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为一轮或一系列，被用来指日子的循环。

items.en: Wice named a week, while the older seofonnihte, seven nights, still served in law.
items.cn: wice 指一周，而更古老的 seofonnihte（七夜）在法律中仍在使用。

items.en: Week replaced the older counting form and became the ordinary word.
items.cn: week 取代了旧的计法，成为普通用词。

items.en: Compounds such as weekday and weekend fixed the week’s inner shape.
items.cn: weekday、weekend 等复合词固定了一周内部的形状。

items.en: A four-day week and a working week show the word measuring labour.
items.cn: a four-day week 与 working week 显示这个词可以衡量劳动。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like week, the second names neighbouring spans of time.
note.cn: 第一组与 week 形近音近，第二组是相邻的时间段。

entries.definition: Happening once every week.
Any day from Monday to Friday.
Saturday and Sunday.
Not strong, the same sound but different sense.
Two weeks, fourteen nights.
A period of about thirty days.
A fixed period of study or office.
Any length of time marked off.

normalIntro.en: Keep week as seven days first, then let compounds split it into work and rest.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住 week 是七天，再由复合词把它分成劳作与休息。

normal.en: Week is the span; weekday and weekend divide it.
normal.cn: week 是整段，weekday 与 weekend 把它分开。

normal.en: Weekly is the adjective and adverb.
normal.cn: weekly 是形容词也是副词。

normal.en: Do not confuse week with weak.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 weak 混淆。

normal.en: Within a week means before seven days pass.
normal.cn: within a week 意为七天之内。

normal.en: Week by week describes slow, steady change.
normal.cn: week by week 描述缓慢而稳定的变化。

abstract.en: Picture seven torn pages lying in a heap.
abstract.cn: 想七张撕下的纸堆在一起。

abstract.en: Feel the corner of the pad curl as you tear.
abstract.cn: 感受撕页时纸本边角卷起。

abstract.en: See a fresh page appear above the notes.
abstract.cn: 看笔记上方又出现一张新纸。

examples.en: We stayed in the mountains for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在山里待了一个星期。

examples.en: The shop opens late twice a week.
examples.cn: 这家店每周有两次开得晚。

examples.en: She has a busy week ahead of her.
examples.cn: 她接下来一周很忙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威克」——威克家的挂历一撕七页，就是一周，撕完一圈再从头。

root: 日耳曼语词根（一轮、一系列）→ 古英语 wice（一周）→ 中古英语 week；同源词有 weekday、weekend、weekly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as seven days, narrows to the calendar frame and the working week, then works inside compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从七天出发，缩窄到日历框架与工作周，再在复合词里发挥作用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: seven torn calendar pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：七张撕下的日历页。

branches.en: The span branch: a course lasting six weeks.
branches.cn: 长度分支：持续六周的课程。

branches.en: The calendar branch: due by the end of the week.
branches.cn: 日历分支：周末前到期。

branches.en: The work branch: a four-day week and a week of offers.
branches.cn: 工作分支：四天工作周与一周的优惠。

branches.en: The compound branch: plans that change at weekends.
branches.cn: 复合分支：周末变化的计划。

branches.en: The origin branch: a turn of the days.
branches.cn: 起源分支：日子的一轮。

intro.en: Week compounds with day, end and mid to place events, and takes -ly as an adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: week 与 day、end、mid 复合以标定时间，并加 -ly 作形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 周末；（离家）度周末
definition_en: Saturday and Sunday, when most people do not work, and to spend such a period somewhere
core_image: 周五傍晚的车站，人们拎着包往家赶，脸上已经有了松弛的样子
scene: 周五最后一节课结束，楼道里全是拖着行李箱的人，大家都想着回家过周末。By four on Friday the corridors were full of people leaving for the weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 weekend 是「周末」（第 1 个义项：周六与周日这段休息时间）；句意为周五四点走廊里挤满赶回家过周末的人。周五傍晚车站里拎包赶路的人群就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 周末出游的人；周末小屋

senses.title: Saturday and Sunday
senses.definition: the two days at the end of the working week
senses.definitionCN: 工作周末尾的两天
senses.example: We usually go walking at the weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 我们通常在周末去散步。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the pair of days when work stops.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：工作停止的那两天。

senses.title: The time off around those days
senses.definition: the period of rest that begins on Friday evening and ends on Sunday night
senses.definitionCN: 从周五晚上到周日夜里这段休息时间
senses.example: The whole weekend was ruined by rain.
senses.exampleCN: 整个周末都被雨毁了。
senses.why: In speech the weekend stretches to include Friday night and Sunday evening.
senses.whyCN: 口语里周末扩展到包括周五夜与周日夜。

senses.title: A three-day holiday of this kind
senses.definition: a weekend lengthened by a public holiday, often called a long weekend
senses.definitionCN: 因公共假日而延长的周末，常说 long weekend
senses.example: They took a long weekend in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山里度过了一个长周末。
senses.why: Add a public holiday to Saturday and Sunday and the weekend grows by a day.
senses.whyCN: 在周六周日上加一个公共假日，周末就多出一天。

senses.title: To spend a weekend somewhere
senses.definition: to stay somewhere for the weekend, often used with away or in
senses.definitionCN: 在某地度过周末，常与 away 或 in 连用
senses.example: They weekended in a cottage by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在湖边小屋度周末。
senses.why: The noun turned verb means simply passing the period in a place.
senses.whyCN: 名词变动词，只表示在某地度过这段时间。

senses.title: A weekly paper or edition
senses.definition: in publishing, the weekend edition of a paper
senses.definitionCN: 报纸的周末版
senses.example: The story ran in the weekend edition.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇报道登在周末版上。
senses.why: Papers name an edition by the period it covers, so weekend labels the Saturday issue.
senses.whyCN: 报纸按所覆盖的时段命名版面，周末版便指周六那一期。

intro.en: Weekend is a recent English compound, put together in the nineteenth century when the working week took its modern shape.
intro.cn: weekend 是近代英语复合词，形成于十九世纪，当时工作周才具备现代形态。

items.en: The two halves are old: wice meant a week and ende meant an end.
items.cn: 两个部分都很古老：wice 指一周，ende 指末端。

items.en: Weekend first described the time between Saturday work and Monday morning in industrial towns.
items.cn: weekend 起初描述工业城镇里从周六下班到周一早晨的这段时间。

items.en: Shorter hours and cheap rail travel turned the weekend into a break away from home.
items.cn: 工时缩短与廉价铁路让周末成为离家休憩的时间。

items.en: British usage prefers at the weekend, American prefers on the weekend.
items.cn: 英式多用 at the weekend，美式多用 on the weekend。

items.en: The verb to weekend is rare but standard, as in they weekend by the sea.
items.cn: 动词 to weekend 少见但标准，如他们在海边度周末。

note.en: The first group is the weekend family, the second the neighbouring periods.
note.cn: 第一组是 weekend 词族，第二组是邻近时段。

entries.definition: The other half of the week.
A person who spends weekends away.
The act of spending a weekend away.
Happening once a week.
A day or period of no work, often longer.
A short pause in work or study.
The first day of the weekend.
The second day of the weekend.

normalIntro.en: The word is just week plus end, so the sense is visible on the page.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 week 加 end，意思在字面上看得见。

normal.en: At the weekend in Britain, on the weekend in America.
normal.cn: 英国的 at the weekend，美国的 on the weekend。

normal.en: A long weekend adds a holiday Monday.
normal.cn: long weekend 是把周一假日一并算入。

normal.en: A weekender is a person or a small house.
normal.cn: weekender 可指人，也可指周末小屋。

normal.en: Weekend as a verb needs a place or the word away.
normal.cn: weekend 作动词要接地点或 away。

normal.en: Weekday is the opposite half of the week.
normal.cn: weekday 是一周中相反的另一半。

abstract.en: Picture a station platform at six on Friday.
abstract.cn: 想周五六点的站台。

abstract.en: Hear suitcase wheels on concrete.
abstract.cn: 听箱轮压在水泥地上。

abstract.en: Feel a coat come off the shoulders.
abstract.cn: 感受外套从肩上脱下。

examples.en: We are going to the coast for the weekend.
examples.cn: 我们周末去海边。

examples.en: It rained all weekend, so we stayed in.
examples.cn: 整个周末都在下雨，我们没出门。

examples.en: They weekended at a small hotel near the border.
examples.cn: 他们在边境附近的一家小旅馆度周末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威肯德」——威肯德周五一下班就把包拎走，说一周的尽头就是休息。

root: week（古英语 wice，一周）+ end（古英语 ende，末端），十九世纪复合而成；同源词有 weekday、weekender。

sensesIntro.en: The compound starts as two rest days, stretches to the whole break, lengthens into a long weekend and becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个复合词先指两天休息，扩展到整段休息，延成长周末，再变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a Friday platform full of travellers.
core.cn: 核心意象：周五傍晚挤满乘客的站台。

branches.en: The two days branch: walking at the weekend.
branches.cn: 两日分支：周末去散步。

branches.en: The break branch: rain ruining the whole time.
branches.cn: 休憩分支：被雨毁掉的整段时间。

branches.en: The long branch: a holiday Monday added on.
branches.cn: 延长分支：加上周一的假日。

branches.en: The verb and edition branch: weekending by a lake, a weekend edition.
branches.cn: 动词与版本分支：湖边度周末与周末版。

branches.en: The origin branch: week plus end.
branches.cn: 起源分支：week 加 end。

intro.en: Weekend is a compound of two old words and takes the ordinary -er and -ing forms.
intro.cn: weekend 由两个古老词复合而成，采用普通的 -er 与 -ing 形式。

latinIntro.en: The word is English-built, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语自造，故拉丁表留空。

items.meaning: more than one, or he weekends

definition_zh: 哭泣；流泪；（伤口）渗液
definition_en: to shed tears because of sadness or strong feeling, and of a wound, to let fluid run out slowly
core_image: 一个人背靠墙坐着，眼泪直往下走，衣襟却一点声音都没有
scene: 散场后影院里只剩一个人，灯亮了，他还坐着，眼睛一点点红起来。She wept quietly after the film ended, without making a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 weep 是「哭泣」（第 1 个义项：因悲伤或强烈情绪而流泪）；句意为电影结束后她静静地哭，一点声音都没有。靠着墙坐着、眼泪直往下走的人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 哭泣；流泪；（伤口）渗出液体

derivatives.zh: weep 的过去式与过去分词

senses.title: To shed tears
senses.definition: to produce tears from the eyes because of grief or strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤或强烈情绪而从眼中流泪
senses.example: She wept as she read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她读那封信时哭了。
senses.why: This is the core sense, usually quieter and more literary than cry.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，通常比 cry 更静、更书面。

senses.title: To cry for someone or something
senses.definition: to mourn or grieve over a person or event
senses.definitionCN: 为某个人或某件事哀伤
senses.example: They wept for the loss of their old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为失去老师而哭。
senses.why: With for or over the verb names the cause of grief, not just the tears.
senses.whyCN: 接 for 或 over 时，动词指向悲伤的缘由，而不只是眼泪。

senses.title: To cry with joy or relief
senses.definition: to shed tears from an emotion other than grief
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤之外的情绪而流泪
senses.example: Her parents wept with joy at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，她的父母喜极而泣。
senses.why: The tears are the same, so the verb covers any strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 眼泪是一样的，所以这个动词可以覆盖任何强烈的情绪。

senses.title: Of a wound, to run with fluid
senses.definition: of a sore or wound, to discharge liquid slowly
senses.definitionCN: 指疮口或伤口慢慢流出液体
senses.example: The cut on his hand was still weeping.
senses.exampleCN: 他手上的伤口还在渗液。
senses.why: Something that keeps letting drops out looks like a crying eye.
senses.whyCN: 不停滴出东西的物体，像一只流泪的眼睛。

senses.title: To hang downwards
senses.definition: of branches, to droop or hang down, usually in the form weeping
senses.definitionCN: 指枝条下垂，多用 weeping 形式
senses.example: A weeping willow bent over the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 一株垂柳弯在池塘上方。
senses.why: Drooping branches are said to weep, as if they were crying.
senses.whyCN: 下垂的枝条被说成在哭，仿佛它们也在流泪。

intro.en: Weep goes back to Old English wēpan, a Germanic word for crying out and lamenting, and it still carries a quieter, older tone than cry.
intro.cn: weep 可上溯到古英语 wēpan，是日耳曼语中呼喊与哀悼的词，至今仍比 cry 带着更静、更古的意味。

items.en: The root meant to cry out, and related words in other Germanic tongues mean to weep as well.
items.cn: 这一词根意为高声呼喊，其他日耳曼语言中的相关词也表示哭泣。

items.en: Wēpan meant to lament, often aloud, and the strong past wēop became wept.
items.cn: wēpan 意为哀叹，常是出声的，其强变化过去式 wēop 成为 wept。

items.en: The word lost its loud sense while cry took over, and weep settled as the quieter word.
items.cn: 这个词失去了高声义，cry 接替了它，weep 成为更静的用法。

items.en: The wound sense, recorded from the fifteenth century, uses the image of dripping.
items.cn: 伤口义自十五世纪有记录，用的是滴落的意象。

items.en: Weeping willow names a tree whose branches hang like falling tears.
items.cn: weeping willow 指枝条垂落如泪的树。

note.en: The first group shares the weep forms, the second gives the words that sit beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是 weep 的形式与派生，第二组是与它并列的词。

entries.definition: The ordinary past and participle.
entries.definitionCN: weep 的过去式与过去分词

entries.definition: Crying, or hanging down.
A person who weeps, or a hired mourner.
entries.definitionCN: 哭泣的人；雇来的哭丧者

entries.definition: Inclined to cry, or a film that makes one cry.
The everyday word, often louder and with sound.
To cry with short, gasping breaths.
To feel and show deep grief, often publicly.
To cry out with a long, high sound.

normalIntro.en: Weep is the quiet form of crying, and the word also lets a wound and a willow do it.
normalIntro.cn: weep 是哭泣里安静的那种，伤口与柳树也能用它。

normal.en: The past is wept, not weeped.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wept，不是 weeped。

normal.en: Weep over the cause, weep for the person.
normal.cn: weep over 指的是缘由，weep for 指的是那个人。

normal.en: Weep with joy says the tears are glad ones.
normal.cn: weep with joy 说明眼泪是欢喜的。

normal.en: A weeping wound keeps running.
normal.cn: weeping wound 是不断渗液的伤口。

normal.en: A weeping willow is named for its hanging branches.
normal.cn: weeping willow 因垂枝得名。

abstract.en: Picture a face turned away from the light.
abstract.cn: 想一张背过光去的脸。

abstract.en: Feel the line of wet on a collar.
abstract.cn: 感受领口那道湿痕。

abstract.en: Hear no sound at all.
abstract.cn: 听不到一点声音。

examples.en: He wept when he heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到消息时他哭了。

examples.en: The child wept over the broken toy.
examples.cn: 孩子为弄坏的玩具哭了。

examples.en: The sore on his arm had begun to weep.
examples.cn: 他臂上的疮开始渗液。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维普」——维普先生靠墙坐着，眼泪安静地流，一点哭声也没有。

root: 日耳曼语词根（呼喊）→ 古英语 wēpan（哀叹、哭泣，过去式 wēop）→ weep / wept；同源词有 weeping、weepy。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts as quiet tears, widens to grief and to joy, then lends itself to dripping wounds and drooping trees.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从安静的眼泪出发，扩展到悲伤与喜悦，再借给渗液的伤口与下垂的枝条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face against a wall, wet and silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着墙、湿了脸却无声。

branches.en: The tears branch: reading a letter through tears.
branches.cn: 眼泪分支：读信时落泪。

branches.en: The grief and joy branch: mourning a teacher, weeping at good news.
branches.cn: 悲喜分支：哀悼老师，喜极而泣。

branches.en: The wound branch: a cut that keeps running.
branches.cn: 伤口分支：不断渗液的伤口。

branches.en: The tree branch: branches hanging over still water.
branches.cn: 树木分支：垂在静水上的枝条。

branches.en: The tear and wound branch: both are liquid that keeps running.
branches.cn: 泪水与伤口分支：两者都是不停流下的液体。

intro.en: Weep keeps an irregular past and takes -ing, -er and -y in the ordinary way.
intro.cn: weep 保留不规则过去式，并按常规加 -ing、-er 与 -y。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; Latin expressed the same idea with flere, which survives in English borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；拉丁语用 flere 表达同一概念，其痕迹见于英语借词。

definition_zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使烦恼
definition_en: to measure how heavy something is, to have a stated weight, and to think carefully about choices
core_image: 老式天平两端各放一只盘，指针在刻度间来回摆动最后停住
scene: 集市上卖水果的老板把袋子放上秤盘，指针一晃，最后停在一个数上，他报出价来。The seller put the bag on the scale to weigh it and waited for the needle to settle.
sceneCN: 这里 weigh 是「称重」（第 1 个义项：测量某物有多重）；句意为摊主把袋子放上秤，等指针停稳。两端摆动的天平与指针就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使忧心

senses.title: To measure weight
senses.definition: to find out how heavy something is, using a scale
senses.definitionCN: 用秤查明某物有多重
senses.example: The nurse weighed the baby at every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每次来访都给婴儿称重。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the balance answers a question of heaviness.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：天平回答「有多重」的问题。

senses.title: To have a stated weight
senses.definition: to be of a particular heaviness
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个特定的重量
senses.example: This parcel weighs almost two kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包裹重近两公斤。
senses.why: The verb takes the weight as its own measure, so no object is needed.
senses.whyCN: 动词自身带上重量，因此不需要宾语。

senses.title: To think about choices
senses.definition: to compare facts or options carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前仔细比较事实或选项
senses.example: The committee weighed the risks before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在投票前权衡了风险。
senses.why: A balance holds two pans, and a mind holds two options the same way.
senses.whyCN: 天平托着两只盘，头脑也同样托着两个选择。

senses.title: To be a burden on someone
senses.definition: to trouble or oppress a person’s mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某人心里烦恼、沉重
senses.example: The decision weighed on her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定压在她心上好几周。
senses.why: Something heavy presses down, so worry is said to weigh on a mind.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的东西会向下压，于是忧虑被说成压在心头。

senses.title: To raise a ship’s anchor
senses.definition: of a ship, to lift the anchor before sailing
senses.definitionCN: 指船在启航前把锚拉起
senses.example: The fleet weighed anchor at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在黎明起锚。
senses.why: A phrase from sailing, kept because anchor and balance share the idea of lifting.
senses.whyCN: 这是航海用语，因为起锚与天平共通「抬起」的意象而保留。

intro.en: Weigh comes from Old English wegan, to carry or to lift, the same root that gives wagon and the Latin vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: weigh 来自古英语 wegan（搬运、抬起），与 wagon 及拉丁语 vehere（运载）同根。

items.en: The root meant to move or carry a load, and weighing was done by lifting and comparing.
items.cn: 这一词根意为移动或承载，古时称量靠抬起并比较。

items.en: Wegan meant to carry, to lift and to weigh, all in one verb.
items.cn: wegan 一名兼指搬运、抬起与称量。

items.en: The spelling weigh appeared, and the past form became weighed under French-influenced habits.
items.cn: 拼写 weigh 出现，过去式在法语影响下成为 weighed。

items.en: The weighing of evidence extended the word to judgement and decision.
items.cn: 权衡证据把词义扩展到判断与决断。

items.en: Weight, the noun, came from the same root and now names the thing measured.
items.cn: 名词 weight 出自同根，如今指被测量的那份东西。

note.en: The first group shares the weigh root and shape, the second the words used in measuring and deciding.
note.cn: 第一组与 weigh 同根形近，第二组是测量与决断中的近义词。

entries.definition: How heavy a thing is, or a piece of metal used to weigh.
Heavy, or serious and important.
The act of measuring or judging.
A road or method, the same sound.
To find the size or amount of something.
To think about something before deciding.
To judge the value or quality of something.
To load someone with a heavy duty or worry.

normalIntro.en: Start with the balance, then let it tilt into decisions and into worry.
normalIntro.cn: 先看天平，再让它倾斜出去，成为决断与忧虑。

normal.en: Weigh is the verb; weight is the noun.
normal.cn: weigh 是动词，weight 是名词。

normal.en: Weigh about ten kilos needs no object.
normal.cn: weigh about ten kilos 不带宾语。

normal.en: Weigh the options means put each one on the balance.
normal.cn: weigh the options 就是把每个选择放上天平。

normal.en: Weigh on someone means press down on the mind.
normal.cn: weigh on someone 是压在某人心上。

normal.en: Weigh anchor is the opposite of drop anchor.
normal.cn: weigh anchor 与 drop anchor 相反。

abstract.en: Picture a needle swinging and dying away.
abstract.cn: 想指针摆动后慢慢停住。

abstract.en: Hear the small click of a brass weight set down.
abstract.cn: 听铜砝码落下时轻轻一响。

abstract.en: Feel one side sink and the other rise.
abstract.cn: 感受一头下沉、一头升起。

examples.en: Please weigh this parcel before you post it.
examples.cn: 寄之前请称一下这个包裹。

examples.en: She weighs less than she did last year.
examples.cn: 她比去年轻了些。

examples.en: You must weigh the cost against the benefit.
examples.cn: 你必须把成本与收益权衡一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——摊主喊一声「喂」，把袋子往秤上一放，看指针停在哪。

root: 日耳曼语词根（搬运、抬举）→ 古英语 wegan（搬、抬、称）→ weigh；同根词有 weight、wagon，拉丁语 vehere。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts at the balance, states a weight, then moves to weighing options, to weighing on a mind, and to lifting an anchor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从天平出发，报出重量，再转为权衡选择、压在心头，最后是起锚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle settling.
core.cn: 核心意象：停住的秤针。

branches.en: The measure branch: weighing a baby and weighing two kilos.
branches.cn: 测量分支：给婴儿称重与重两公斤。

branches.en: The judgement branch: comparing risks before a vote.
branches.cn: 判断分支：投票前比较风险。

branches.en: The burden branch: a decision that presses for weeks.
branches.cn: 负担分支：压了数周的决定。

branches.en: The sailing branch: anchor lifted at dawn.
branches.cn: 航海分支：黎明起锚。

branches.en: The scale and the mind share one image: two pans, then two choices.
branches.cn: 天平与头脑共用一个意象：两只盘，两个选择。

intro.en: Weigh takes regular endings and the noun weight from the same root.
intro.cn: weigh 用规则词尾，名词 weight 出自同一词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin vehere means to carry, and the table shows how the same image spread.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 vehere 意为运载，拉丁表展示同一意象的扩散。

items.meaning: to carry, to lift, to weigh

definition_zh: 奇怪的；怪异的；离奇的；（古）命运的
definition_en: very strange and hard to explain, often in a way that makes people uneasy
core_image: 街角的路灯忽明忽暗，路口站着一个人影，看不清脸
scene: 夜里回家时，楼道灯一间间亮起又灭掉，脚步声总在身后多一下，他回头看却没有人。That night the corridor felt weird; every light went out just behind him.
sceneCN: 这里 weird 是「奇怪的」（第 1 个义项：非常怪异、难以解释，且常令人不安）；句意为那晚走廊里感觉怪怪的，灯总在他身后熄灭。忽明忽暗的灯与看不清脸的人影就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Very strange and unsettling
senses.definition: unusual in a way that is hard to explain and slightly disturbing
senses.definitionCN: 异于寻常、难以解释且略带不安
senses.example: There was a weird smell in the empty flat.
senses.exampleCN: 空屋子里有一股怪味。
senses.why: This is the modern core: strange plus a slight shiver.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代核心义：奇怪外加一点发凉。

senses.title: Strange in an interesting way
senses.definition: strange in a way that is odd but engaging
senses.definitionCN: 怪得有趣、引人好奇
senses.example: The shop sells weird and wonderful lamps.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖各种离奇有趣的灯。
senses.why: The same strangeness can charm rather than chill, which gives the phrase weird and wonderful.
senses.whyCN: 同一种怪可以是迷人也可是骇人，于是有了 weird and wonderful。

senses.title: Behaving oddly
senses.definition: of a person, acting in an odd or puzzling way
senses.definitionCN: 指人行为反常、令人费解
senses.example: He has been weird all week, not answering messages.
senses.exampleCN: 他这一周都很古怪，消息也不回。
senses.why: The same strangeness turns outward, so odd behaviour carries the word of the uncanny.
senses.whyCN: 同一种怪转向人本身，于是古怪的行为也带上了这个诡异之词。

senses.title: Feeling unwell
senses.definition: in informal use, feeling faint or unwell
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指感到不适、发虚
senses.example: I felt weird after the second cup of coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 第二杯咖啡之后我觉得不太舒服。
senses.why: A body that feels strange is described with the word for anything strange.
senses.whyCN: 身体感觉不对劲，就用了形容任何怪异之物的词。

senses.title: Fateful, in older use
senses.definition: in old literature, having power over fate
senses.definitionCN: 古文学中指尖有掌控命运之力
senses.example: The weird sisters appear before the king.
senses.exampleCN: 命运三姐妹出现在国王面前。
senses.why: This is the original sense, from the noun weird meaning fate, later softened to fateful.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义，来自名词 weird（命运），后来淡化为「关乎命运的」。

intro.en: Weird first meant fate, from Old English wyrd, and the modern sense of strange grew out of the idea of a fateful, uncanny power.
intro.cn: weird 本义是「命运」，来自古英语 wyrd；现代的「奇怪」义由「带着命运感、超乎自然的力量」生长而来。

items.en: Wyrd meant fate or destiny, the power that decides what happens to a person.
items.cn: wyrd 意为命运，决定一个人遭遇何事的那个力量。

items.en: The root is the same as the verb become, so fate was the word for what turns out.
items.cn: 这一词根与动词 become 同源，命运便指最终成为的样子。

items.en: The weird sisters of fate were the three goddesses who spin a life’s thread.
items.cn: 中古英语中 the weird sisters 是纺出人生之线的三位女神。

items.en: In Macbeth the weird sisters are witches, and weird took on the sense of uncanny.
items.cn: 在《麦克白》里 the weird sisters 是女巫，weird 由此带上诡异之意。

items.en: The adjective weakened from uncanny to simply strange and odd.
items.cn: 这个形容词从诡异淡化为单纯的奇怪、古怪。

note.en: The first group is the weird family, the second the adjectives of strangeness.
note.cn: 第一组是 weird 词族，第二组是表示奇怪的形容词。

entries.definition: In a strange way.
The quality of being strange.
A person seen as strange.
Fate, the original sense.
The plain word for unfamiliar or odd.
Slightly unusual or peculiar.
Strange in a way that frightens.
Strange in a way that seems supernatural.

normalIntro.en: Remember the old sense first: weird was fate, and only later came to mean strange.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住旧义：weird 本来是命运，后来才变成「奇怪」。

normal.en: Weird is the adjective; weirdly and weirdness follow.
normal.cn: weird 是形容词，weirdly、weirdness 随之而来。

normal.en: A weirdo is a strange person, short and informal.
normal.cn: weirdo 是怪人，简短而口语。

normal.en: Weird and wonderful pairs oddness with charm.
normal.cn: weird and wonderful 把古怪与迷人配在一起。

normal.en: Feel weird means feel unwell, not see ghosts.
normal.cn: feel weird 是不舒服，不是见鬼。

normal.en: The weird sisters in Macbeth are the Three Witches.
normal.cn: 《麦克白》里的 weird sisters 就是三女巫。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp flickering above an empty corner.
abstract.cn: 想路灯在空街角上忽明忽暗。

abstract.en: Hear one extra footstep behind you.
abstract.cn: 听身后多出一步脚步。

abstract.en: Feel the small chill on the back of the neck.
abstract.cn: 感受后颈那一点涼。

examples.en: It is weird to see the square so empty.
examples.cn: 看到广场这么空，感觉很奇怪。

examples.en: She had a weird dream about a door in the sea.
examples.cn: 她做了一个怪梦，梦见海里有一扇门。

examples.en: The whole afternoon felt weird around him.
examples.cn: 他身边的整个下午都透着古怪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威德」——威德夜里回家，路灯一盏盏在身后灭掉，他说这真够怪的。

root: 古英语 wyrd（命运，同根于 become）→ 中古英语 weird sisters（命运三女神）→ 莎士比亚后转为「诡异」→ 现代「奇怪」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as fate, darkens into uncanny power, then lightens into ordinary strangeness.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从命运出发，变暗成诡异的力量，再变轻为平常的「奇怪」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp flickering over an empty corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：空街角上明灭的灯。

branches.en: The strange branch: a smell in an empty flat.
branches.cn: 怪异分支：空屋里的一股怪味。

branches.en: The charming branch: weird and wonderful lamps.
branches.cn: 迷人分支：离奇有趣的灯。

branches.en: The personal branch: queer behaviour and a body that feels odd.
branches.cn: 个人分支：古怪行为与不适的身体。

branches.en: The fate branch: the weird sisters of old literature.
branches.cn: 命运分支：旧文学里的命运姐妹。

branches.en: The charm and the fate branch: both keep the old shiver of the uncanny.
branches.cn: 迷人分支与命运分支：两者都留着那点古旧的诡异寒意。

intro.en: Weird is a bare adjective that takes the ordinary -ly, -ness and -o endings.
intro.cn: weird 是光杆形容词，采用普通的 -ly、-ness 与 -o 词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 欢迎；迎接；受欢迎的；可随意使用的
definition_en: to greet someone in a friendly way, and to be gladly received or freely allowed
core_image: 院门被推开，主人快步迎出来，伸手接过客人的行李
scene: 第一次到同学家，他母亲在门口等着，接过包，说路上辛苦了，快进来。His mother met me at the door, took my bag and welcomed me inside.
sceneCN: 这里 welcome 是「欢迎」（第 1 个义项：友善地迎接某人）；句意为他母亲在门口接了我，接过包把我迎进屋。推门而出、伸手接手提行李的主人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；可随意使用的

collocations.zh: 欢迎来到我们这座城市

senses.title: To greet someone gladly
senses.definition: to meet a person in a friendly way and show that one is glad they came
senses.definitionCN: 友善地迎接某人，并表现出对他们的到来感到高兴
senses.example: They welcomed the guests at the gate with tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口用茶迎接客人。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the friendly meeting at arrival.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：到访时友善的迎接。

senses.title: To be glad to accept
senses.definition: to receive an idea, a change or a gift with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地接受某个想法、变化或礼物
senses.example: We welcome any suggestions for the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乐于接受对新计划的任何建议。
senses.why: A change can be greeted as a guest is, so the verb spreads to things.
senses.whyCN: 变化也能像客人一样被迎进来，于是动词扩展到事物。

senses.title: Received with pleasure
senses.definition: of news or events, gladly received
senses.definitionCN: 指消息或事件令人高兴
senses.example: The rain was welcome after a month of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 热了一个月之后，这场雨很受欢迎。
senses.why: The adjective describes what people would be glad to greet.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述人们乐于迎接的东西。

senses.title: Freely permitted to use
senses.titleCN: 可随意使用的；受欢迎的（人）
senses.definition: of a person, allowed to do or take something without asking
senses.definitionCN: 指人无需请示即可使用或取用
senses.example: You are welcome to stay for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 欢迎你留下吃晚饭。
senses.why: To be welcome somewhere is to be free of the usual barrier.
senses.whyCN: 在某处受欢迎，就是不受通常的界限阻挡。

senses.title: A greeting of arrival
senses.definition: the act of greeting, usually warm, in the noun form
senses.definitionCN: 名词形式，带来暖意的迎接行为
senses.example: They gave us a warm welcome at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站给了我们热烈的欢迎。
senses.why: The friendly meeting at the gate turned into a noun, so it became a thing one gives.
senses.whyCN: 门口那场友善的相见转为名词，于是成了一份可以送出的东西。

senses.title: A polite reply
senses.definition: a fixed reply to thanks, meaning there is no need to thank
senses.definitionCN: 对道谢的固定回答，意为不必谢
senses.example: “Thank you.” “You’re welcome.”
senses.exampleCN: “谢谢。”“不用谢。”
senses.why: The reply says the favour was freely given, so no debt remains.
senses.whyCN: 这句答语表示这份好意是白送的，因此不欠什么。

intro.en: Welcome is Old English wilcuma, a compound of will and come, meaning a guest whose coming is wished for.
intro.cn: welcome 是古英语 wilcuma，由 will 与 come 复合而成，意为「来得合人心愿的客人」。

items.en: Wilcuma named a desired guest, someone whose arrival pleased the host.
items.cn: wilcuma 指备受期盼的客人，其到来使主人高兴。

items.en: The first element is will, the wish, and the second is come, so the word literally means wished-coming.
items.cn: 第一部分是 will（意愿），第二部分是 come，字面即「如人所愿的到来」。

items.en: The noun was reshaped under the influence of French bienvenu and gave a verb welcome.
items.cn: 名词受法语 bienvenu 影响而变形，并衍生出动词 welcome。

items.en: The adjective sense of freely allowed appeared, as in you are welcome to try.
items.cn: 形容词「可随意」的义项出现，如 you are welcome to try。

items.en: You are welcome as a reply to thanks is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「不用谢」这一答语自十九世纪有记录。

note.en: The first group shares the welcome shape, the second gives the words used at a greeting.
note.cn: 第一组与 welcome 形近同族，第二组是迎接时的近义词。

entries.definition: Friendly to guests, or the act of greeting.
Not wanted or gladly received.
One who greets others.
The Old English ancestor, a wished-for guest.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语本源：受期盼的客人

entries.definition: To say hello to someone in a friendly way.
To meet and admit a guest, often formally.
Friendly care shown to guests.
To take what is offered.

normalIntro.en: Say the word slowly: will plus come, a coming that someone wishes for.
normalIntro.cn: 慢慢念这个词：will 加 come，一次有人盼望的到来。

normal.en: Welcome is verb, adjective and noun all at once.
normal.cn: welcome 可作动词、形容词和名词。

normal.en: You are welcome is the fixed reply to thanks.
normal.cn: You are welcome 是对道谢的固定回答。

normal.en: A warm welcome is the noun after an adjective.
normal.cn: a warm welcome 是形容词加名词。

normal.en: Unwelcome news is news nobody wanted.
normal.cn: unwelcome news 是没人想要的消息。

normal.en: Make someone welcome means put them at ease.
normal.cn: make someone welcome 是让某人自在。

abstract.en: Picture a gate swung open from inside.
abstract.cn: 想门从里面被推开。

abstract.en: Feel a bag lifted out of your hand.
abstract.cn: 感受手里的包被接走。

abstract.en: Hear the door close warmly behind you.
abstract.cn: 听门在身后温和地关上。

examples.en: They welcomed us with tea and fruit.
examples.cn: 他们用茶和水果欢迎我们。

examples.en: Your comments are welcome at any time.
examples.cn: 随时欢迎您提出意见。

examples.en: “Thanks for the lift.” “You’re welcome.”
examples.cn: “谢谢你载我一程。”“不客气。”

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维尔康」——维尔康先生每到门口就说：来得好，欢迎进屋。

root: 古英语 wilcuma（will 意愿 + cuma 来者，即受期盼的客人）→ 中古英语受法语 bienvenu 影响成 welcome。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a wished-for arrival, becomes the act of greeting, then any glad acceptance and even the answer to thanks.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「如人所愿的到来」出发，成为迎接的行为，再扩展到任何乐意的接受，乃至道谢的答语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a host taking a guest’s bag at the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：主人在门口接过客人的包。

branches.en: The greeting branch: guests met at the gate and a warm welcome.
branches.cn: 迎接分支：门口迎客与热烈欢迎。

branches.en: The acceptance branch: suggestions and rain both welcome.
branches.cn: 接受分支：建议与雨都受欢迎。

branches.en: The permission branch: you are welcome to stay.
branches.cn: 许可分支：欢迎你留下。

branches.en: The reply branch: you’re welcome.
branches.cn: 答语分支：不用谢。

branches.en: The host and the permission branch: one opens a door, the other a choice.
branches.cn: 主人分支与许可分支：一个开门，一个放行。

intro.en: Welcome is a very old compound that can now be a verb, an adjective or a noun.
intro.cn: welcome 是很古老的复合词，如今可作动词、形容词或名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin used gratus and acceptare for being welcome, and the table gives those cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 gratus 与 acceptare 表示受欢迎与被接受，拉丁表给出这些亲族词。

definition_zh: 福利；幸福；福利救济；（动物的）康乐
definition_en: the health and happiness of people, and the help the state gives to those in need
core_image: 社区服务站的窗口前排着队，柜台上摆着一叠表格和一支笔
scene: 社区服务站早上九点开门，窗口前排着队，有人来问孩子的补贴怎么申请。People come to the welfare office to ask about help with rent.
sceneCN: 这里 welfare 是「福利」（第 1 个义项：人的健康与幸福，以及由此而来的救济）；句意为人们到福利办事处询问房租方面的援助。排着队的窗口与一叠表格就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 福利；幸福；福利救济；康乐

senses.title: Health and happiness
senses.definition: the well-being of a person or group, in body and in life
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体在身体与生活上的良好状态
senses.example: Parents are responsible for their children’s welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 父母对孩子的生活安康负有责任。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense and still the widest: how well someone is doing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、也最宽泛的义项：一个人过得如何。

senses.title: State help for those in need
senses.definition: money or services given by the state to people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 国家给予需要者的钱款或服务
senses.example: The family lived on welfare for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人靠救济生活了两年。
senses.why: The general sense narrowed to the organised system that secures it.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛的义项收窄为保障它的那套制度。

senses.title: Organised care in a system
senses.definition: the whole set of policies and services for people’s well-being
senses.definitionCN: 为人的福祉而设的全部政策与服务
senses.example: The report compares welfare in five countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告比较了五个国家的福利制度。
senses.why: The personal good scaled up to a whole national arrangement, and the word followed it.
senses.whyCN: 个人的好处放大为整套国民安排，这个词也随之跟上。

senses.title: The good of animals
senses.definition: the condition of animals kept by people, especially farm animals
senses.definitionCN: 尤其是农场动物在人类饲养下的状况
senses.example: The farm was praised for its animal welfare standards.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场因动物福利标准受到称赞。
senses.why: The same care owed to people was extended to the animals people keep.
senses.whyCN: 原本对人负有的照料，被扩展到人所饲养的动物身上。

senses.title: A service for a group
senses.definition: used before a noun for services for students or workers
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指面向学生或职工的服务
senses.example: The union runs a welfare fund for members.
senses.exampleCN: 工会为会员设有一项福利基金。
senses.why: From the system came the smaller units that pay out, the fund and the office.
senses.whyCN: 从制度里长出付款的小单位：基金与办事处。

intro.en: Welfare is a modern compound of well and fare, literally the state of faring well, and it began in Middle English.
intro.cn: welfare 是 well 与 fare 的近代复合词，字面即「过得好」的状态，始于中古英语。

items.en: Fare meant to journey or to get on, so faring well meant prospering.
items.cn: fare 意为行走或进展，因此 faring well 就是过得兴旺。

items.en: Welfare first meant the condition of being happy and prosperous, close to our well-being.
items.cn: welfare 最初指幸福兴旺的状态，接近今天的 wellbeing。

items.en: As cities grew, welfare came to mean organised help for the poor.
items.cn: 随着城市发展，welfare 转而指对穷人的有组织帮助。

items.en: The welfare state made the word the name of a national system.
items.cn: 福利国家一词让这个词成为一种国民制度的名称。

items.en: Animal welfare extended it to creatures that cannot claim help themselves.
items.cn: animal welfare 把它扩展到无法自己主张帮助的生灵。

note.en: The first group is the welfare family, the second the nouns it is often set against.
note.cn: 第一组是 welfare 词族，第二组是常与之对照的名词。

entries.definition: Belief in state welfare provision.
Health and happiness in general.
Fare well, said at parting.
To get on, or the price of a journey.
Money paid by the state, or an advantage.
Help given voluntarily to those in need.
The state of being healthy and happy.
Looking after someone who needs it.

normalIntro.en: Welfare is plain English underneath: to fare well is to get on well, and welfare is that state.
normalIntro.cn: welfare 底下是很平常的英语：fare well 就是过得好，welfare 就是这个状态。

normal.en: Well plus fare: the fare is the travel, so fare well is to get on well.
normal.cn: well 加 fare：fare 是行走，fare well 就是走得顺。

normal.en: On welfare is American for living on benefit.
normal.cn: on welfare 是美式说法，指靠补助生活。

normal.en: The welfare state is the whole system, not one office.
normal.cn: the welfare state 是整套制度，不只是某个办事处。

normal.en: Well-being is the close twin; welfare took the official sense.
normal.cn: well-being 是近亲，welfare 承担了官方色彩。

normal.en: Animal welfare uses the same word for creatures kept by people.
normal.cn: animal welfare 用同一个词指人类饲养的动物。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a service-office window.
abstract.cn: 想服务窗口前排起的队。

abstract.en: Feel the edge of a form under your fingers.
abstract.cn: 感受指尖压着表格的硬边。

abstract.en: Hear a clerk explain a form line by line.
abstract.cn: 听窗口职员一行行解释表格。

examples.en: The school looks after the welfare of every pupil.
examples.cn: 学校关心每个学生的福祉。

examples.en: The new rules on animal welfare are stricter.
examples.cn: 新的动物福利规定更为严格。

examples.en: Many families depended on welfare during the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机期间许多家庭依赖救济。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维尔费」——维尔费先生在服务站排了队，他说这只为把日子过好一点。

root: well（古英语 wel，好）+ fare（古英语 faran，行走、进展）→ 中古英语 welfare；同根词有 farewell、well-being。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a condition of faring well, then names the help that secures it, the system that gives it, and finally the good of animals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「过得好」的状态出发，继而为保障它的帮助、提供它的制度命名，最后扩展到动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue at a welfare office window.
core.cn: 核心意象：福利办事处窗口前的队伍。

branches.en: The well-being branch: parents responsible for a child.
branches.cn: 福祉分支：父母对孩子的责任。

branches.en: The help branch: a family living on welfare.
branches.cn: 救济分支：靠救济生活的家庭。

branches.en: The system branch: a report comparing five countries.
branches.cn: 制度分支：比较五国的报告。

branches.en: The animal and fund branch: farm standards and a union fund.
branches.cn: 动物与基金分支：农场标准与工会基金。

branches.en: The well-being and help branch: the same good, once described and once given.
branches.cn: 福祉与救济分支：同一份好，一处描述、一处给予。

intro.en: Welfare is a native compound of two Old English words and takes only the ordinary noun endings.
intro.cn: welfare 是两个古英语词的本土复合，只采用普通名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is English-built, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语自造，故拉丁表留空。
